overview: The two main types of lymphocytes driving adaptive immunity, split by whether they fight pathogens using antibodies or direct cell action.
genZNote: B cells: the antibody factory. T cells: the direct-action strike team.

aspects.label: Type of Immunity Mediated
aspects.valueB: Cell-mediated immunity — directly attacks infected/abnormal cells or helps coordinate the response.

aspects.label: Effector Form
aspects.valueA: Differentiates into plasma cells, which secrete antibodies.
aspects.valueB: Differentiates into helper T cells, cytotoxic T cells, or regulatory T cells.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: B for Bone marrow, T for Thymus — the classic mnemonic for where each lymphocyte matures.
overlay.memoryTrick: B cells make antiBodies. T cells are the Thymus-trained fighters.
overlay.commonMisconception: B cells don't directly kill infected cells — that job belongs to cytotoxic T cells; B cells fight via secreted antibodies instead.
